title: Kidnapped By A Beast Girl
description: Kidnapped and transported to a primitive world, I built a civilization from the ground up.

seasons.title: Season 1
seasons.description: The complete saga of building a civilization in a wild land.

parts.text: When I regained consciousness, I found myself lying in the heart of a dense, primordial forest. A tall, fierce warrior woman—resembling an Amazon—had captured me and dragged me to a tribe of primitive women who hadn't even discovered fire yet. Upon seeing me, the Chieftain immediately designated me as 'breeding stock.' My only advantage in this savage new world? I had at least finished middle school. The sharp pain of hitting the hard ground jolted me fully awake. There were no asphalt roads, no skyscrapers, and no sounds of urban life—only massive ferns as large as umbrellas and thick, humid air that smelled of damp earth.

parts.text: The scent of decaying leaves filled my nostrils as I struggled to make sense of my surroundings. Suddenly, the ground trembled, and a shadow loomed over me. Standing before me was a girl, at least six feet tall, clad only in rough animal skins. Snowy white furry ears sat atop her head, and a long tail flicked restlessly behind her. She tilted her head, scanning me from head to toe with the cold, calculating focus of a predator, as if determining whether I was edible. She muttered to herself, noting my lack of fur and claws and the paleness of my skin.

parts.text: Without warning, she grabbed me by my jeans and hoisted me into the air with a single hand as if I were weightless. I tried to explain that I was human, but she told me to shut up or she'd cut out my tongue. She slung me over her shoulder like a sack of rice and began to run. Her name was Aru. She was incredibly fast, each stride covering several meters. My stomach slammed against her hard shoulder blade with every step. Along the way, a black beetle as large as a washbasin scurried out of the grass. Without breaking her stride, Aru kicked it, sending it flying until it burst into a sticky mess.

A tiny ember glowed for a split second before dying out. I had failed. Aru woke up behind me. Seeing the thin trail of smoke, she panicked. I reached out slowly and scratched the base of her furry ears. Her entire body stilled, and a soft purr escaped her throat. She melted like butter, and the crisis was averted.

parts.text: I sat atop the beast's broad back as the tribe dragged it home. Dozens of warriors pulled and shouted, and when the elders and children waiting at the village gate saw the massive corpse blocking half the entrance, they fell silent. Then, the Chieftain raised her fist and roared that tonight, everyone would eat their fill. That night, everyone fell asleep in a happy heap by the bonfire, warm and full. However, I woke up early the next morning and inspected the leftovers.

parts.text: Aru was at the front of the line, her spear dancing as she picked off any centipede that tried to bypass the fire. She fought with a ferocity I hadn't seen before, her tail stiff and her ears pricked forward. When the last of the swarm finally retreated into the darkness, the clearing was silent except for the crackling of the dying fires and the heavy breathing of the warriors. Not a single person had been bitten. The tribe let out a collective roar of victory that could be heard for miles.

parts.text: The Chieftain walked over to me, her face soot-stained but smiling. She placed a hand on my shoulder and announced to everyone that I was no longer just 'breeding stock'—I was the 'Heart of the Tribe.' My brain had saved them from a threat their muscles couldn't touch. Aru rushed over and practically tackled me, licking the soot from my face with even more enthusiasm than before. This time, I didn't pull away. I realized that in this wild, dangerous world, I had found a home and a family that valued me for exactly who I was.

parts.text: As the stars came out, the tribe gathered around the fire, eating the first pieces of smoked meat from our reserves. We were no longer just survivors; we were becoming a civilization. I looked at Aru, whose head was resting on my lap, and then at the Chieftain and the children practicing with their slings. My journey had started with a kidnapping, but it was ending with me becoming a leader. The primitive forest was still dangerous, but with fire, spears, and a bit of science, we were ready for whatever came next.
